text: dsh-enhance 是面向 DSH Web 和 Desktop composition 的对话界面增强插件。它将浏览器端模块挂载到 DSH 的 shell.overlay，并接入会话、工作区和会话输入服务。用户可在新建会话前设置标题、从 Files 侧栏拖入文件或文件夹引用、编辑并在新分支重发最后一条提示词、通过时间线跳转长对话，并用悬浮面板调整对话宽度和界面开关。适合希望更快整理和浏览 DSH 对话的用户；需要兼容的 DSH 0.2.x Web composition，文件引用还需要 Files 侧栏。

dsh-enhance adds session naming, file references, prompt editing with branch resend, a message timeline, and floating chat-width controls to DSH Web/Desktop. It mounts in DSH's shell overlay. Requires compatible DSH 0.2.x; file references need the Files sidebar.
我想在创建新会话时先写好标题。
能不能把工作区里的文件直接拖到输入框引用？
上一条提示词写错了，我想修改后重新发送。
长对话里怎样快速跳到之前某一轮？
我想把聊天区域调宽一点，并快速开关界面功能。
新建会话时能否跳过命名，继续使用原来的流程？
我希望拖入文件夹时插入可供对话引用的目录路径。
Can I rename a new conversation before it opens?
I need a quick way to jump between questions in a long chat.
How can I correct my last prompt and send it in a fresh branch?
dsh-enhance 的功能「新建会话命名」：点击工作区的加号后输入标题，再创建并打开新会话；也可跳过命名。
dsh-enhance 的功能「文件拖拽引用」：从 Files 侧栏把文件或目录拖到输入框，插入相对路径引用，不会复制文件。
dsh-enhance 的功能「编辑并重发」：点击最后一条提示词旁的编辑按钮，修改文本后发送到从原轮次之前分出的新会话。
dsh-enhance 的功能「消息时间线」：右侧轨道按用户提问显示节点，悬停可预览，点击节点可跳转到该轮对话。
dsh-enhance 的功能「悬浮快捷面板」：拖动悬浮球调整位置，点击后可调节对话宽度并切换时间线、命名等选项。
dsh-enhance 将界面设置保存在当前浏览器的 localStorage 中，包括宽度、时间线及新会话命名开关。

The missing conversation power-up for DeepSeek Harness ✨

New-conversation naming, file drag references, edit-and-resend for the last prompt, a message timeline, and a draggable floating ball with chat-width control for the DSH Web GUI.

dsh-enhance README · Introduction：> I use DeepSeek Harness every day. New sessions need useful names; finding a message in a long thread means scrolling; referencing a file means copying its path; correcting the last prompt should be quick. > > So I built **dsh-enhance**: it leaves DSH’s native structure alone and just makes the daily actions smoother.

dsh-enhance README · ✨ Features：| | Feature | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ✏️ | **New conversation naming** | Name it from the workspace `+` before creating it |
| 📎 | **File drag reference** | Drag a file or folder into the composer as an `@path` |
| ✍️ | **Edit & resend** | Stop a turn, edit the sent prompt inline, and send it again |
| 📍 | **Message timeline** | Scan, preview, and jump through long threads |
| 🫧 | **Floating ball & width** | Everyday tools one click away; 38–90rem live width |
dsh-enhance README · ✨ Features：> The GIFs below are recordings from DSH. The UI may look different with another theme or window size.

dsh-enhance README · ✏️ New Conversation Naming：**Name it before you create it.** Clicking `+` on a workspace title row opens a naming dialog instead of creating another “New Session”.

- Type a name and press Enter; **Skip naming** keeps the native one-click flow.
- The name is written as the conversation title; before the first turn, the sidebar blank row shows it.
- Turn **Name new conversations** off in the quick panel to restore the native behavior.
dsh-enhance README · ✏️ New Conversation Naming：
dsh-enhance README · 📎 File Drag Reference：**Drop a file, get a reference.** Open the **Files** tab in the right sidebar and drag a file or folder row into the composer:

dsh-enhance README · 📎 File Drag Reference：- The composer shows **Drop to reference <name>**; on release it inserts an `@relative/path` chip.
- The file is not moved, copied, or rewritten; the model reads it through its file tools when you send.
- Paths are relative to the conversation workspace root; paths with spaces use `@"..."`.
- Folders are inserted with a trailing `/` (`@path/`) so the model can browse the directory.
- The composer gets an accent outline while dragging; dropping elsewhere inserts nothing.
dsh-enhance README · 📎 File Drag Reference：

dsh-enhance README · ✍️ Edit & Resend the Last Prompt：**Stop, tweak, send again.** When the conversation is idle, a **pencil** appears beside Copy in your last sent prompt’s action row. Clicking it expands the prompt into a full-width inline editor with Cancel / Send:

dsh-enhance README · ✍️ Edit & Resend the Last Prompt：- Edit the text, then click **Send** (or press Enter; Shift+Enter inserts a line, Esc cancels).
- Sending forks the conversation **before the turn that carried that prompt** — including the queued inbox copy — sends the edited text into the new branch, and opens it.
- The branch keeps the earlier history and title. The original is archived when archiving succeeds; otherwise it remains in the conversation list.
- Attachments are not resent; the editor warns when the original prompt had one.

dsh-enhance README · ✍️ Edit & Resend the Last Prompt：> DSH's log is append-only and has no public "rewrite this message" call, so the edit is a **fork before the turn + resend**, not an in-place mutation. The new conversation gets a new Session ID.

dsh-enhance README · 📍 Message Timeline：**Never lose your place in a long thread.** A thin fixed timeline sits on the right:

- One node per question/answer turn; each node is anchored on the user question and covers the assistant reply.
- Hover a node for the question, turn, and a content preview.
- Click a node to jump to the question; the top/bottom buttons jump to the first/last.
- The `>` button collapses the rail; turn it off/on in the quick panel.
dsh-enhance README · 📍 Message Timeline：
dsh-enhance README · 🫧 Floating Ball & Chat Width：**Everyday tools, one click away.** Drag the floating ball anywhere; click it to open the quick panel:

dsh-enhance README · 🫧 Floating Ball & Chat Width：| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Chat width** | Live 38–90rem, default **48rem**, one-click reset |
| **Message timeline** | Toggle the right timeline rail |
| **Native turn navigation** | Hide the horizontal turn rail DSH draws on the right (on by default) |
| **Name new conversations** | Toggle the workspace `+` naming dialog |
| **Floating ball position** | Reset to the default corner |

dsh-enhance README · 🫧 Floating Ball & Chat Width：Width syncs both ways with DSH’s native drag handle: dragging the handle updates the panel value; adjusting the panel writes DSH’s width preference (`dsh.conversation.contentWidth`).

dsh-enhance README · Requirements：- DeepSeek Harness `0.2.1-rc.2` or a compatible 0.2.x Web composition.
- Official Web / Desktop composition (includes `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace`).
- File drag reference also needs the right-sidebar **Files** tab (included in the official composition).
- Works with both the desktop app and `dsh web`.

dsh-enhance README · Clone this repository (or download and extract its ZIP), then:：cd dsh-enhance
pnpm install
pnpm build
dsh plugin --profile desktop add .
```

For the Web profile, use `dsh plugin --profile web add .` instead. Reload the Web page or fully restart the desktop app after installing.

dsh-enhance README · ❓ FAQ：
Does dragging a file move or upload it? No. The plugin only writes the existing path as an `@relative/path` reference into the draft. The file stays where it is; the model reads it through its file tools when you send.
Why don’t I see the features after installing?

dsh-enhance README · ❓ FAQ：Confirm the plugin is installed in the target profile, then reload the page; on desktop, fully quit and restart the app. Also confirm DSH is `0.2.1-rc.2` or a compatible 0.2.x.
Why is the timeline sometimes missing? The timeline relies on the Chat view’s `data-chat-flow-*` markers; the Trajectory view does not have them. If a message sits inside a collapsed “process” group, you may need to expand that group after jumping.

dsh-enhance README · ❓ FAQ：
Does editing the last prompt create a new conversation? Yes. DSH keeps an append-only log, so the plugin forks before the prompt’s turn and sends the edited text in the new branch. The branch keeps the earlier history and title. The old conversation is archived if possible; if archiving fails, it remains in the list. Attachments from the original prompt are not resent.

dsh-enhance README · ❓ FAQ：
Where are settings stored? Only in the current browser: `dsh-enhance.state.v1` stores width, timeline/naming switches, and the floating ball position; `dsh.conversation.contentWidth` is shared with DSH. Nothing is uploaded to a server.
Does the plugin collect data? No. There is no telemetry or external reporting; conversations, file paths, and settings stay local.
